title_en: Oh Tell Me, Tell Me, Girl Kalina
en_note: Machine translation by Claude (my reading), not on Pesna.org and not checked by a native speaker. Treat it as a study aid.
translator_notes: Dialect forms (като зема, един пат, оште) look Bulgarian-influenced. 'Оште непроносила' read as 'that has not yet laid eggs', my reading; 'Ќе удра... ќе броја' (strike, count) is my reading.

lines.en: - Oh tell me, tell me, girl Kalina,
what do you feel like eating?

lines.cyr: - Мене ми се јаде печена погача,
lines.lat: - Mene mi se jade pečena pogača,
lines.en: - I feel like eating baked flatbread,
- Oh tell me, tell me, girl Kalina,
what do you feel like eating?

lines.cyr: - Мене ми се јаде печена кокошка,
lines.lat: - Mene mi se jade pečena kokoška,
lines.en: - I feel like eating a roast hen
- Oh tell me, tell me, girl Kalina,
what do you feel like drinking?

lines.cyr: - Мене ми се пие тригодишно вино,
lines.lat: - Mene mi se pie trigodišno vino,
lines.en: - I feel like drinking three-year-old wine,
- Oh, I will take a cornel-wood stick,

lines.cyr: три пати ќе удра, един пат ќе броја,
lines.lat: tri pati ḱe udra, edin pat ḱe broja,
lines.en: three times I will strike, one time I will count,

lines.cyr: па да видим' што ти се пие!
lines.lat: pa da vidim' što ti se pie!
lines.en: and then we will see what you feel like drinking!
